name: Better Enums
listed_description: Reflective enums (to string, iteration). Single header.
reason: The only measurement is doc/Performance.md: compile-time ratio of a file declaring 36 Better Enums (647 constants) to a file that only includes iostream (clang 3.6 fast constexpr 0.66, full constexpr 2.25; gcc 5.1 1.58 and 4.23; VC2015RC 1.18). iostream is a yardstick, not a competing enum library, and most ratios are above 1 (slower than iostream). DesignDecisionsFAQ.md and OptInFeatures.md only compare the library with its own earlier data-structure attempts. No comparison with magic_enum, a hand-written switch, std::string_view tables or another enum library found in the repo, docs, or search (pistack.xyz and feedbagel.com posts were blocked).

name: clReflect
reason: README and doc/MarkingPrimitivesForReflection.md carry only qualitative statements (constant-time stringless GetType, memory-mapped database that loads quickly); no numbers and no baseline. No benchmark directory in the repo and no comparison found by search.

name: config-loader
listed_description: A C++17 static reflection framework, from parse configuration file to native data structure.
reason: README claims lightweight (under about 1000 lines) and flexible, nothing about speed. No benchmark directory, no performance mention in README or the three open issues; it wraps tinyxml2, jsoncpp and yaml-cpp and does not compare against them.

name: CPP-JWT
listed_description: JSON Web Token library for C++.
reason: README makes no performance claim (focus is ease of use); it bundles nlohmann/json as a dependency rather than competing with it, and the repo has no benchmark directory. A search for cpp-jwt versus jwt-cpp or libjwt timings found no benchmark.

name: CPP-Reflection
reason: README is build instructions and a pointer to the author's blog (austinbrunkhorst.com, blocked by the egress policy); no numbers, no benchmark directory, no baseline in the repository.
